page.overview:
What is Skellig?

Isma's mother told Guts and his company about the flow of time on the island being different outside its shores. As explained by Danan, a night in the outside world equated to a few days in Skellig. According to Danan, the island had an affinity that comprised its inhabitants and dictated whether outsiders were welcome. Its inhabitants were able to notice the appearance of Griffith, Danan included.

Skellig's shore was steep and rocky, featuring coves and cliffs. Further on land, it was guarded against outsiders via different means, such as barriers. One such warding measure was an enchanted field with scarecrows and animated pumpkins, chiefly using the power of gnomes. The island proper housed a village of mages. Nearby, the territories closer to the Flower Storm Monarch brimmed with a vast od. These territories, known as Elfhelm, comprised a dense, barytes-lacking forest inhabited by astral creatures (up and including fauns, unicorns, elves, centaurs and wind-aligned beings) as well as a massive spirit cherry tree which doubled up as the seat of the Flower Storm Monarch. Underneath, the cherry tree featured a "magic mushroom bed" made of fungi which had drawn plenty of spiritual energy from its roots. The roots of the spirit tree also housed the mausoleum of the Lady Priestess of the Cherry Blossoms.

The island also featured a ravine that led to a dimly lit gorge that was populated by astral beings of a darker disposition as well as the witch Volvaba. Schierke likened it to a dark enclave, namely Qliphoth. The gorge also housed a so-called forest of stone, a barytes-cramped location where dwarves lived and worked.

According to the Skull Knight, its foundations and masters of the place were a blob similar to the one that rose in Albion during the Incarnation Ceremony. As explained by Puck, the island belonged to the Interstice. Being unrecorded in the Western Sea, regular humans could not reach it. According to Schierke, though originally supposed to exist in the Astral World, it ended overlapping the physical one after the Great Wave of the Astral World. Thus, pirates and other humans started reaching it from the physical world. Despite this, at one point in the past, a legendary group of sea warriors (their name misremembered by Danan as "Vikins") were able to reach the island. The warriors had their armors and weapons swiped and magicked into golems. Molda tells Schierke that the island was attacked long ago by a large nation in the continent. Captured soldiers were sacrificed, and their souls were used to animate wicker men.
